gen.title: From descent measurements to lift and drag
gen.orderNote: Steps follow the measurement to calculation order shown on the page.

steps.label: steady (constant velocity and no acceleration) descent
steps.quote: If a glider is in a steady (constant velocity and no acceleration) descent, it loses altitude as it travels.
steps.orderHint: Follow the flight data to the force solution.

steps.label: tangent tan of the glide angle a
steps.quote: The tangent tan of the glide angle a is equal to the change in height h divided by the distance flown d:
steps.orderHint: Follow the flight data to the force solution.

steps.label: tan(a) = h / d
steps.orderHint: Follow the flight data to the force solution.

steps.label: lift L times the cosine cos of the glide angle
steps.quote: The lift L times the cosine cos of the glide angle plus the drag D times the sine sin of the glide angle is equal to the weight W:
steps.orderHint: Follow the flight data to the force solution.

steps.label: lift times the sine of the glide angle
steps.quote: The lift times the sine of the glide angle is equal to the drag times the cosine of the glide angle.
steps.orderHint: Follow the flight data to the force solution.

steps.label: experimentally determine the lift and drag
steps.quote: With these three equations we can experimentally determine the lift and drag of a glider.
steps.orderHint: Follow the flight data to the force solution.
